title: The general chart presentation has exactly power-torsion kernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $s\ge1$, and $a,a_2,\ldots,a_s\in R$, with no regularity assumption. Put $I=(a,a_2,\ldots,a_s)$, $S=R[y_2,\ldots,y_s]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $J=(ay_i-a_i\mid 2\le i\le s)$ and $Q=S/J$. Let $B=R[I/a]\subseteq R_a$ be the $R$-subalgebra generated by $x/a$ for $x\in I$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. The assignments $[y_i]\mapsto a_i/a$ induce a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:Q\to B$, and $$\ker\phi=\{x\in Q\mid \exists N\ge0,\ a^Nx=0\}.$$

source.place: Tag 0G8S (lemma-affine-blowup-quotient-description), statement and proof; the finite-support denominator argument is the explicit elementary realization retained from the parent.

proof.text: By the polynomial universal property evaluate $y_i$ at $a_i/a$ in $R_a$. Its image lies in $B$. Each relation evaluates to $a(a_i/a)-a_i=0$. Thus $\phi([f])=f(a_2/a,\ldots,a_s/a)$ is well defined: changing $f$ by $\sum_i h_i(ay_i-a_i)$ changes its evaluation by zero. Evaluation preserves sums, products and constants, so this is an $R$-algebra map.

proof.text: Let E be the composite of the quotient evaluation with the chart inclusion into R_a. Show that x/a belongs to the subalgebra range(E) for every x in I by ideal-span induction. For x=a the fraction is 1; for x=a_i it is E([y_i]); zero, addition and scalar multiplication preserve membership because (r*x)/a=(r/1)*(x/a). Therefore every adjoin generator of B belongs to range(E). Since B is generated by these fractions, B is contained in range(E); injectivity of the subtype inclusion gives surjectivity onto B.

source.place: Tag 0G8S (lemma-affine-blowup-quotient-description), statement; direct finite-support proof using the fractions of Tag 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text: Prove the constant-multiple identity by polynomial induction, implemented by the proved private helper presentation_constant_multiple. For a constant r use exponent zero. If a^n[p]=[r] and a^m[q]=[t], then a^(n+m)[p+q]=[a^m*r+a^n*t]. If a^n[p]=[r], the quotient relation a[y_i]=[a_i] gives a^(n+1)[p*y_i]=[r*a_i]. Thus every polynomial representative p has a^n[p]=[r] for some n and r in R. Applying E gives (a/1)^n E([p])=r/1.

source.place: Tag 0G8S (lemma-affine-blowup-quotient-description), statement; direct finite-support proof using the fractions of Tag 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text: If $\phi(z)=0$, step 3 gives $b/1=0$ in $R_a$. The defining fraction equivalence gives $a^k b=0$ in $R$ for some $k\ge0$. Hence $a^{d+k}z=a^k[b]=0$ in $Q$. Conversely, if $a^Nz=0$, applying $\phi$ gives $(a/1)^N\phi(z)=0$ in $R_a$. Multiplication by the unit $(a/1)^{-N}$ gives $\phi(z)=0$ there and thus in the subalgebra $B$. This proves the asserted equality of kernels.
